title: The Workshop Cabinet
question_on_image:
Which padlock isn't
keeping things shut?
rules_on_image:
Drawers slide straight out. Only these locks hold them shut.
No damage or unlocking.
x_caption: A, B or C? Name the padlock that isn't doing its job—and explain why.
answer: B. The two middle drawers can slide open together while B remains locked.
explanation: There are four stacked drawers and three locked hasps. A connects the fixed cabinet frame to the top drawer. C connects the bottom drawer to the fixed base. Both prevent their attached drawers from opening. B crosses the gap between the two middle drawers: its upper mounting plate belongs to the second drawer, and its lower mounting plate belongs to the third. It joins two moving parts without attaching either to the cabinet frame. Pulling those two drawers forward together preserves the position of every part of the closed hasp and padlock. B therefore fails to keep them shut. Pulling either middle drawer alone would resist the connection, which makes B initially appear effective.
decisive_step: Recognize that crossing a drawer gap does not necessarily anchor a lock to the cabinet. Both of B's mounting points move forward together.

alternatives_checked.why_rejected: Its upper mounting plate is visibly on the continuous fixed top rail; its lower plate is on drawer 1. Opening that drawer would separate the two mounting surfaces.
Its upper mounting plate is on drawer 4; its lower plate is visibly on the continuous fixed bottom rail. The bottom rail cannot accompany the drawer.

alternatives_checked.candidate: B is secure because neither middle drawer opens independently
alternatives_checked.why_rejected: The drawers can move together. Their relative positions remain unchanged, so the locked connection does not obstruct their shared movement.

difficulty_rationale: My assessment, without human testing. All three closed hasps plausibly cross a gap. The reader must identify the surfaces supporting each mount, then mentally move two drawers together. Difficulty comes from this change of viewpoint rather than small details or specialist knowledge.
scene_concept: A furniture restorer's workshop contains one handsome oak cabinet with four stacked drawers. Three matching locked hasps are labelled A, B and C. The middle hasp connects two drawer fronts instead of securing either to the fixed frame.
